stories.title: Mention agents in ticket comments

acceptance_criteria: a mentioned agent answers in the ticket thread

stories.notes: Board revision 0007 adds comment_mention_jobs (unique per comment and agent, role snapshot, response_comment_id) and card_events for the ticket event stream. CommentService saves the comment first, MentionService resolves enabled agents from @[Name] or bare @Name, queues one job per mention on an in-process executor and writes the answer as a normal agent comment. Retry is refused for active or answered jobs, so a retry never duplicates the comment. Ticket SSE publishes agent_started/agent_completed/agent_failed with Last-Event-ID replay; the card dialog completes mentions, shows job states and offers Retry. Suite: 137 backend, 19 vitest, 22 Playwright.

stories.title: Answer human discussion messages automatically
stories.description: A human message in a roundtable or autonomous thread starts one background round; in a manual thread an explicit @agents or participant mention does the same, and the reply box says so.

stories.notes: DiscussionService._auto_run requests one round after the message commits (background, rounds=1). Explicit triggers reuse extract_mentions from the mention service plus an @agents token. Only human actors trigger; agent-authored messages never loop. UI: mode-aware placeholder and a manual-mode hint. Tests: test_run_control.py (roundtable, autonomous, @agents, participant name, manual/closed stay idle). Suite: 144 backend, 19 vitest, 22 Playwright.

stories.title: Recover interrupted work and explain skipped replies
stories.description: Startup reconciliation for runs and mention jobs, an explicit auto_run outcome on discussion messages, and the overview scope aligned with the board list.
acceptance_criteria: a run left running or paused by a restart becomes failed with process_restart and its thread returns to idle

the client explains a skipped automatic answer instead of staying silent
GET /discussions/overview requires boards:read in addition to discussions:read
stories.notes: Follows decision 0002 (explicit recovery states). Services.initialize runs recover_async_work after migrations: RunService.recover fails running/paused runs and resets thread run_state, MentionService.recover fails running jobs and resubmits queued ones. DiscussionService.add_message returns auto_run and the reply area shows a toast for already_running/thread_closed/no_participants. The overview now requires boards:read too (API tokens cannot carry discussion scopes today, so this is defence in depth). Tests: test_async_recovery.py (run recovery, job recovery + retry), test_run_control.py (auto_run outcomes incl. an active run), test_discussions.py (overview scope). Suite: 148 backend, 19 vitest, 22 Playwright.

stories.title: Accounts, sessions and key hygiene
stories.description: Make the private install manageable: revocable server-side sessions, password change and reset, administrator-only user CRUD, sign-in throttling, expiring and rotatable API tokens, and re-sealing of provider keys after a secret rotation.
acceptance_criteria: every signed-in account has the same scopes except users:admin and credentials:admin, which stay with the admin role so only admin manages accounts and installation-wide API keys
logout, password change, role change and disabling an account revoke stored sessions; expired sessions are purged at startup
an administrator can create users, change roles, disable accounts and reset passwords, and the last enabled admin cannot be demoted or disabled
repeated failed sign-ins are throttled per username and client address with retry_after_seconds
API tokens expire after 90 days by default, can be rotated, and can never hold credentials:admin or users:admin
provider keys sealed with TRALALA_PREVIOUS_SECRET_KEY are re-sealed with the current secret at startup
the first admin password is written to <data>/.bootstrap-password instead of the log, and weak session secrets are replaced by a per-install secret
Settings exposes the password form, the admin-only Users card and token rotation
stories.notes: Migration 0005 adds user_credentials.role and the sessions table. core/context.py owns ROLE_SCOPES; has_scope is now explicit so nothing is implicit. New: api/v1/users.py, LoginThrottle, AgentService.reseal_credentials. Docs: decisions/0007, api.md, database.md, architecture.md, README, .env.example. Follow-up: members also lost credentials:admin, so the global API keys are admin-only and the Settings credentials card is hidden for members.

stories.title: Theme kits with light and dark palettes
stories.description: Bring the CareNomad and MatchMap visual languages into the app as selectable theme kits, each with a dark and a light palette and its own pulsing CSS motion, without changing the font or layout.
acceptance_criteria: Settings offers a theme kit choice (CareNomad, MatchMap) and the existing dark/light/system mode
each kit has both a dark and a light palette defined as semantic CSS variables
the ambient background and the wordmark pulse animate per kit and stop under prefers-reduced-motion
the font stack, layout and component markup are unchanged and no web fonts are fetched
the kit choice persists in localStorage and survives a reload
stories.notes: data-theme-kit selects the kit, data-theme the mode. AmbientBackground renders grid, glow, three blobs and stars; CareNomad breathes over 5.2s/16s, MatchMap pings over 2.8s with a 22s wash. docs/decisions/0008 records the scope (colour + motion only). Follow-up: MatchMap no longer recolours CareNomad's ambient layers; it paints a dot field, ten twinkling particles and a sliding gradient wash (22 s), while CareNomad keeps its breathing line grid and drifting fields.

stories.title: Per-account appearance and the classic kit
stories.description: Keep the original flat palette as an extra theme kit and store the appearance choice per account so one person's theme never shows for another.
acceptance_criteria: Classic kit reproduces the original palette in both modes and disables the ambient layer and pulse
theme_mode and theme_kit are stored on the signed-in account and returned by /auth/me
GET and PUT /auth/preferences work for user sessions only; API tokens are rejected
a second account on the same browser starts from the default kit instead of inheriting the previous choice
the preference survives a new login and is validated against the known kits and modes
stories.notes: Migration 0006 adds theme_mode/theme_kit to user_credentials. ThemeProvider applies the account value on sign-in and PATCHes on change; localStorage stays as a first-paint cache. Tests: four backend preference tests, a vitest classic case and an E2E account-isolation check.
